theory.title: Have/get something done: encargar un servicio
theory.explanation: Usa have/get + objeto + participio cuando organizas que otra persona realice un servicio por ti. El foco está en el servicio recibido, no en quién hace el trabajo: I had my suitcase repaired (mandé reparar mi maleta).
theory.tip: No significa que tú hagas el trabajo: organizas que alguien lo haga.

content.passage: Before leaving for a long holiday, Daniel organised several services. He had his passport photo taken at a local shop and got his suitcase repaired because one wheel was broken. He also had his travel documents translated. His sister was having her bicycle serviced, so they collected it together. These arrangements saved time and helped them avoid problems on the first day.

items.prompt: Describe a service you have arranged recently.
items.modelAnswer: I enjoy travelling because it gives me the chance to discover new places and understand different ways of life. One experience I remember clearly was a journey that did not go exactly as planned. At first, I felt a little worried, but I asked for information and found a practical solution. I learned that preparation is important, although it is also useful to stay flexible. In the future, I would like to explore more destinations and learn about their local traditions.

content.audioTranscript: A: We are planning a trip next month. B: Where are you going? A: We are travelling to a historic town. B: Have you booked the journey? A: Yes, and we have printed the tickets. B: Which station will you use? A: The central one. B: Is there a local guide? A: Yes, we made a booking online. B: Do you know the platform? A: It is shown on the app. B: What will you visit? A: The museum and the market. B: Are you learning about local customs? A: Yes, and we are staying at a small hotel. B: Enjoy your arrival!
